The answer is **B**. The act of State doctrine is a rule of judicial restraint. Courts treat the assessment of a foreign State's sovereign conduct, including whether it committed a tort, as a matter for the executive, so they don't rule on it. This is the closer fit of the two options the team note allows, since C says the opposite. I'm changing my earlier answer of D because it doesn't match either option the note gives.

CONFIDENCE: 66
